singular VERSION (commit unknown)

Usage: singular state create [--config FILE] [--state-dir DIR] --blueprint
       FILE --application-policy HEX [--seed TXID#IX] --koios-url URL
       --network-magic N [--koios-token-file FILE] [--network-time DIR]
       [--vault FILE [--passphrase-fd N] | --wallet-address ADDR --bundle FILE
       | --wallet-skey FILE] [--confirm-timeout SECONDS] [--receipt FILE]
       [--trace LEVEL] [--trace-to SINK] [--trace-format FORMAT]

Create the registry of an application

Creates one registry of the application whose policy is given, by spending a
seed output of your wallet, and prints the registry's address, its state token
and the transactions it sent. The first registry of an application publishes
the state validator as a reference script, in a transaction of its own, before
it creates the registry; a later registry finds the live copy and sends one
transaction.

The seed fixes the registry's identity. The wallet funds the transactions and
keeps their change.

A write is signed by exactly one signer: --vault (the normal route),
--wallet-address with --bundle (written for an external signer, ending as
waiting-for-signatures), or --wallet-skey (a key file, legacy). Naming two is
refused.

Available settings:
  Show this help text
  switch: -h|--help

  A JSON file giving the settings the command line and the environment leave
  out.
  option: --config FILE
  env: SINGULAR_CONFIG FILE
  default: singular.json in the working directory, if there is one

  Keep the journal and submissions under DIR.
  option: --state-dir DIR
  env: SINGULAR_STATE_DIR DIR
  config:
    state-dir: # or null
      <string>
  default: the per-user state directory

  The compiled validators (plutus.json) of the release.
  option: --blueprint FILE
  env: SINGULAR_BLUEPRINT FILE
  config:
    blueprint: # or null
      <string>

  The policy of the application the registry is for: 56 hex characters, a
  28-byte hash. It is the one parameter of the state validator.
  option: --application-policy HEX

  The wallet output the registry is booted from; it fixes the registry's
  identity.
  option: --seed TXID#IX
  default: your largest ada-only output

  Base URL of the Koios API used to read the chain and to submit.
  option: --koios-url URL
  env: SINGULAR_KOIOS_URL URL
  config:
    koios-url: # or null
      <string>

  The network: 1 for preprod, 42 for the generated development network.
  option: --network-magic N
  env: SINGULAR_NETWORK_MAGIC N
  config:
    network-magic: # or null
      <string>

  File holding a Koios bearer token; its contents are never printed.
  option: --koios-token-file FILE
  env: SINGULAR_KOIOS_TOKEN_FILE FILE
  config:
    koios-token-file: # or null
      <string>

  Directory with the pinned time-manifest.json, shelley-genesis.json and
  era-history.cbor.
  option: --network-time DIR
  env: SINGULAR_NETWORK_TIME DIR
  config:
    network-time: # or null
      <string>
  default: the preprod recording packaged with the program

  Signer, normal route: sign from this encrypted wallet vault.
  option: --vault FILE
  env: SINGULAR_VAULT FILE
  config:
    vault: # or null
      <string>

  Read the vault passphrase, one line, from this inherited file descriptor; it
  wins over SINGULAR_PASSPHRASE.
  option: --passphrase-fd N
  default: SINGULAR_PASSPHRASE on a development network, else ask on the
  terminal with the echo off

  Signer, external route: stage the run for a signer at this address; goes
  with --bundle.
  option: --wallet-address ADDR

  Signer, external route: the new file the unsigned transactions are written
  to; goes with --wallet-address.
  option: --bundle FILE

  Signer, legacy route: sign with this payment key file. Prefer the vault.
  option: --wallet-skey FILE

  How long each submission may take to confirm; past it the command stops,
  journalled, and never resubmits.
  option: --confirm-timeout SECONDS
  default: 600

  Also write the JSON receipt to FILE.
  option: --receipt FILE

  How much to narrate: off, what (protocol steps) or how (also their
  mechanics).
  option: --trace LEVEL
  env: SINGULAR_TRACE LEVEL
  config:
    trace: # or null
      <string>
  default: what on a terminal, otherwise off

  Where the narration goes: stderr or file:PATH; repeat for several.
  option: --trace-to SINK
  env: SINGULAR_TRACE_TO SINK
  config:
    trace-to: # or null
      <string>
  default: stderr

  The format of the narration: text for a person, json for a program.
  option: --trace-format FORMAT
  env: SINGULAR_TRACE_FORMAT FORMAT
  config:
    trace-format: # or null
      <string>
  default: text on standard error, json in a file

Where settings come from:
  A setting with an env and a config line above is given in any of three ways,
  and the first that is present wins: the flag, then the variable, then the
  key in the config file, then the default.

  The file is one JSON object whose keys are the setting names without their
  dashes, text or numbers, for example

    {"koios-url": "https://preprod.koios.rest/api/v1", "network-magic": 1}

  It is singular.json in the working directory, or the file named by --config
  or SINGULAR_CONFIG. A path in it means what it means on the command line,
  from where the command runs. A passphrase is never read from the file; the
  environment gives one only on a development network, as SINGULAR_PASSPHRASE.

Environment:
  SINGULAR_LOG         A file the protocol phases are appended to, one line
                       each.
  XDG_STATE_HOME       Where the per-user state directory lives (else
                       $HOME/.local/state), under singular/.
  SINGULAR_PASSPHRASE  The vault passphrase, for a development network only: a
                       command on mainnet (764824073), preprod (1) or preview
                       (2) refuses it. --passphrase-fd wins over it, and a
                       value that is empty is refused.

Example:
  singular state create --blueprint plutus.json \
      --application-policy <policy> \
      --koios-url https://preprod.koios.rest/api/v1 --network-magic 1 \
      --vault alice.vault

  With those settings in singular.json instead:
  singular state create --application-policy <policy> \
      --vault alice.vault

Output and exit status:
  Prints one JSON receipt on standard output (--receipt also writes it).
  Exit status 0 on success, 2 for a command line it refused, otherwise the
  outcome class the receipt names: 10 refused before anything was sent,
  11 refused by the ledger, 12 node unavailable, 13 timeout, 14 stale state,
  15 partial, 16 another writer, 17 proof missing, 18 proof inconsistent,
  19 waiting for signatures.
